prompt:
Research the officially documented limits of Tailscale's free Personal plan (users, devices, other limits). Cite Tailscale's own pricing or documentation page and quote the limits.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Tailscale’s Personal plan is documented as free, with six users, unlimited user devices, and several plan-level limits (ACL groups, tagged resources, and ephemeral-resource minutes). The clearest single source is Tailscale’s pricing page; the supporting docs pages confirm the six-user Personal limit and related upgrade behavior.

SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "For individuals who want to securely connect devices, servers, or software. Access nearly all of Tailscale's offerings and products for free, indefinitely." | CLAIM: The Personal plan is Tailscale’s free individual plan.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Unlimited user devices" | CLAIM: The Personal plan does not impose a per-user device cap for ordinary user devices.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Up to 6 users" | CLAIM: The Personal plan allows a maximum of six users.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Up to 3 ACL groups" | CLAIM: The Personal plan is limited to three ACL groups.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Up to 50 tagged resources to start" | CLAIM: The Personal plan includes 50 tagged resources before extra paid add-ons apply.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "1,000 mins per month for ephemeral resources Ephemeral resources enable short-lived workloads like CI/CD runners and Kubernetes pods." | CLAIM: The Personal plan includes 1,000 ephemeral-resource minutes per month for short-lived workloads.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Access nearly all of Tailscale’s features" | CLAIM: The free Personal plan is positioned as including nearly all Tailscale features rather than a separate stripped-down feature set.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Users $0 for up to 6 users" | CLAIM: The pricing table again states that six users are included at no cost on Personal.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "User Devices Computers, phones, etc. Unlimited" | CLAIM: The pricing table distinguishes user devices from tagged/ephemeral resources and marks user devices as unlimited.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Tagged resources Resources like exit nodes, etc. 50 tagged resources included; add more for $1/month each." | CLAIM: Tagged resources beyond the included 50 cost $1 per month each.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "ACL Groups 3" | CLAIM: The Personal-plan ACL group limit is three.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "Basic Tailscale SSH Up to 5 hosts" | CLAIM: Basic Tailscale SSH is limited to five hosts on the Personal plan.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/pricing | QUOTE: "With that in mind, we are currently not enforcing the hard limits or overages of ACL groups, multiple tailnets, tagged resources, and ephemeral resources." | CLAIM: Although these limits are published, Tailscale says it is not currently enforcing hard limits or overages for ACL groups, multiple tailnets, tagged resources, and ephemeral resources.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/docs/account/manage-plans/free-plans-discounts | QUOTE: "The Personal plan permits 6 free users in a single Tailscale network, known as a tailnet." | CLAIM: Tailscale’s docs confirm the Personal plan includes six free users in one tailnet.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/docs/account/manage-plans/free-plans-discounts | QUOTE: "You can also share devices with other users with node sharing." | CLAIM: Device sharing with other users is documented separately through node sharing rather than changing the Personal-plan user limit.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/messages/console/reached-use-limit | QUOTE: "The Personal plan gives you six free users." | CLAIM: Tailscale’s error-message documentation confirms the six-user cap in practical account behavior.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/docs/reference/messages/console/reached-use-limit | QUOTE: "If your tailnet is on the Personal plan, you can upgrade your plan to accommodate more users." | CLAIM: Exceeding the Personal-plan user allowance requires upgrading or removing users.
SOURCE: https://tailscale.com/blog/pricing-v4 | QUOTE: "It now supports up to six users—the same limit Personal Plus had—and includes more of what personal users have increasingly asked for over time." | CLAIM: Tailscale’s pricing-update announcement confirms the Personal plan was expanded to six users.
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: A single official Tailscale page that consolidates every Personal-plan limit in one place, including users, devices, ACL groups, tagged resources, ephemeral minutes, SSH hosts, multiple tailnets, and enforcement status.
